title: TLS and certificates
summary: Inspect an HTTPS server's certificate, learn why a browser trusts it or refuses, and make a PC trust a private certificate authority.

tasks.title: Who vouches for this site?
tasks.text: From **pc**, `curl https://shop.dojo.lab/` refuses to connect. Look at the certificate the server presents. What is the common name (CN) of its **issuer**?
hints: `openssl s_client -connect shop.dojo.lab:443 -servername shop.dojo.lab` performs a TLS handshake and prints the certificate chain. Press Ctrl+C to leave.
Pipe the certificate into `openssl x509` to read it: `openssl s_client -connect shop.dojo.lab:443 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -issuer -subject`.

answer_cmd.cmd: openssl s_client -connect shop.dojo.lab:443 -servername shop.dojo.lab </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -issuer -nameopt RFC2253 | sed 's/^issuer=CN=//'

tasks.title: Which protocol version?
tasks.text: Which TLS version did your handshake negotiate?
hints: `openssl s_client` prints a line like `New, TLSv1.x, Cipher is ...`. `curl -kv https://shop.dojo.lab/` shows it too (`-k` skips verification, for inspection only).

answer_cmd.cmd: openssl s_client -connect shop.dojo.lab:443 -servername shop.dojo.lab </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'TLSv1\.[0-9]' | head -1

tasks.title: Trust the company CA
tasks.text: The issuer is a private CA that your PC does not know, so verification fails. The IT team publishes the CA certificate at `http://10.19.1.10/ca.crt`. Install it into **pc**'s trust store so that plain `curl https://shop.dojo.lab/` (no `-k`) succeeds.

checks.fail_msg: curl https://shop.dojo.lab/ still fails certificate verification.

hints: On Debian, extra trusted CAs go in `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` as `.crt` files. Then run `update-ca-certificates`.

tasks.title: Check out securely
tasks.text: Load the shop over verified HTTPS and submit the order code on the page.

tasks.title: Right certificate, wrong name
tasks.text: `legacy.dojo.lab` points at the same server, yet `curl https://legacy.dojo.lab/` still fails even though you now trust the CA. Read the certificate's **Subject Alternative Name** extension: which DNS name is it valid for?
hints: Read curl's error carefully first: `curl -v https://legacy.dojo.lab/`.

solution.note: The certificate only covers `shop.dojo.lab`. Trusting the issuer is not enough: the name you connected to must also appear in the certificate, otherwise any site with any valid certificate could impersonate any other.

answer_cmd.cmd: openssl s_client -connect shop.dojo.lab:443 -servername shop.dojo.lab </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -ext subjectAltName | grep -o 'DNS:[^, ]*' | cut -d: -f2
